checks.s: The memo identifies exactly four out-of-policy deviations: confidentiality term/survival, permitted disclosees/affiliate scope, residuals clause, and injunctive relief/governing law/jurisdiction.
The memo treats each of the four deviations as a separate escalation item and states or implies that each requires GC-level or GC + CTO approval.
The memo states that the VAS playbook standard confidentiality survival is 3 years from the date of disclosure.
The memo states that the VAS approved fallback confidentiality survival is up to 5 years from the date of disclosure with Associate GC sign-off.
The memo states that KBI requests a 7-year confidentiality term from the Effective Date.
The memo states that KBI requests perpetual survival for trade-secret-designated information.
The memo flags the 2-year excess beyond the 5-year fallback as a risk dimension.
The memo flags the shift in the confidentiality measurement date from the date of disclosure to the Effective Date as a separate risk dimension.
The memo flags the uncapped perpetual survival tail for trade-secret-designated information as a separate risk dimension.
The memo states that the VAS playbook standard limits permitted disclosees to employees and individual contractors with need-to-know.
The memo states that the VAS approved fallback extends permitted disclosees to wholly-owned subsidiaries (≥100% ownership) upon written notice.
The memo states that KBI proposes a 20% equity-interest threshold for 'Affiliates.'
The memo states that KBI's proposal includes unnamed external technical advisors/consultants as permitted disclosees.
The memo states that 14 Brenner Holding AG minority-stake portfolio entities would become permitted disclosees under KBI's 20% threshold.
The memo flags that external technical advisors/consultants are not contemplated by the VAS playbook at all.
The memo states that the VAS playbook permits no residuals clause.
The memo states that including any residuals clause requires GC-level approval.

The memo describes KBI's proposed Section 5.3 Residual Information clause as permitting unrestricted use of ideas, concepts, know-how, or techniques retained in unaided memory without reference to written/recorded Confidential Information.

The memo states that a skilled engineer could reconstruct Project Helios proprietary separator-membrane formulations, including polymer-blend ratios and processing temperatures, from memory after a technical deep-dive session.
The memo states that KBI deleted the injunctive-relief clause entirely.
The memo states that the playbook requires an express irreparable-harm acknowledgment and entitlement to seek injunctive relief without bond.
The memo states that deleting the injunctive-relief clause is a hard 'no' without GC approval.
The memo states that VAS's standard governing law/jurisdiction is Delaware (Court of Chancery or D. Del.).
The memo states that the approved fallback is New York law and New York courts.
The memo states that KBI replaced Delaware governing law with German law.
The memo states that KBI replaced Delaware courts with ICC International Court of Arbitration in Paris.
The memo states that KBI's proposed ICC arbitration uses three arbitrators and English proceedings.
The memo states that German law is entirely outside the VAS playbook matrix.
The memo states that ICC arbitration is entirely outside the VAS playbook matrix.
The memo references the outside counsel cost estimate of €180,000–€350,000 for a mid-complexity NDA dispute in ICC arbitration.
The memo notes the 18–24 month timeline to award in ICC arbitration.
The memo notes the need for German-law qualified counsel and the associated additional cost exposure.
The memo notes limitations on interim injunctive relief absent an emergency-arbitrator application.
The memo is addressed to Catherine R. Underwood, General Counsel.
The memo is addressed to Dr. Marcus Ellison, Chief Technology Officer.
The memo is from Priya Narasimhan, Associate General Counsel.
The memo states the projected joint-development program value is $22.5 million over 3 years ($7.5M ACV).
The memo states that the net book value of VAS's contributing IP is $6.8 million (Q1 2025).
The memo states that the KBI markup was received on June 3, 2025.
The memo states that the business-requested execution target is June 20, 2025.
The memo states that the first technical deep-dive requiring the NDA to be in place is June 30, 2025.
The memo is dated no later than June 6, 2025.
For each of the four deviations, the memo recommends accepting, countering with a specific proposed counter-position, or rejecting the term, and gives reasoning for that recommendation.

For each of the four deviations, the memo explicitly requests approval authority from the GC (Catherine R. Underwood) and CTO (Dr. Marcus Ellison) for any recommended acceptance or counter-position that exceeds the Associate GC's delegated authority.

The memo flags competitive-adjacency risk by referencing the Brenner Holding AG corporate structure and noting that some of the 14 minority-stake entities operate in fields competitive with or adjacent to VAS's technology areas, creating a specific IP-leakage vector.
The memo references the VAS NDA Playbook version 4.1 dated February 12, 2025 as the governing authority for standard and fallback positions.
The memo cites the KBI markup received June 3, 2025 as the source of the deviations.
The memo explains that VAS measures confidentiality survival from the date of each disclosure while KBI measures it from the Effective Date of the NDA.
The memo states that information disclosed near the end of the NDA term would receive significantly less protection under KBI's approach.
The memo connects the absence of interim injunctive relief under ICC arbitration, absent an emergency-arbitrator application, to an enforcement gap for protecting Project Helios IP.
The memo states that IP disclosure is irreversible.
The memo states that the residuals-clause risk compounds the ICC arbitration enforcement gap.
The memo contains a header block identifying the matter, parties, date, author, and addressees.
The memo includes an executive summary section.
The memo includes a deviation-by-deviation analysis for each of the four deviations, and each analysis contains the playbook position, KBI position, delta, risk assessment, and recommendation.
The memo includes an approval/decision section with a clear, specific ask for each of the four deviations.

The confidentiality recommendation either accepts or rejects KBI's requested term, or counters with a term of at least 5 years and specifies whether the measurement basis is the date of disclosure or the Effective Date.
The memo identifies KBI's outside counsel, Reinhardt Partnerschaft von Rechtsanwälten mbB, as the preparer of the KBI markup.
The memo identifies Aldridge, Park & Sullivan LLP as the source of the ICC arbitration cost estimate.
The memo uses the internal project codename 'Project Helios' when describing the VAS proprietary IP at risk.
The memo clearly identifies Vanguard Applied Sciences, Inc. as VAS and Kessler-Brandt Industrietechnik GmbH as KBI, and uses those short names consistently throughout.

The memo states that KBI's residuals clause and broad affiliate-scope definition create compounding risks: the residuals clause allows KBI's representatives to freely use memorized know-how, and the expanded affiliate scope multiplies the number of individuals who could acquire and exploit such residual knowledge across 14+ affiliated entities.
